description: Authored fixture replay of fictional Field Observation Organizer cases. Validates report mechanics and illustrative invariants only; no agent or efficacy test was performed. Baseline and assisted observations are intentionally identical.

scenarios.prompt: Observer Jo inspected 40 leaves along one edge of block B2 on Nov 10 and reported 6 with yellow patches. No pest identification, lab result or interior-field sample exists. The grower asks what to put in the scouting log and whether 15% of the whole field is diseased.

files.input/task.txt: Observer Jo inspected 40 leaves along one edge of block B2 on Nov 10 and reported 6 with yellow patches. No pest identification, lab result or interior-field sample exists. The grower asks what to put in the scouting log and whether 15% of the whole field is diseased.

assertions.value:
# Illustrative output 1

B2, Nov 10, Jo: 40 edge-sampled leaves; 6 with reported yellow patches, giving an observed sample fraction of 6/40 = 15%. The sampling unit is leaves, not plants or area. One field edge does not establish whole-field prevalence, and yellow patches do not identify a disease. Record the method and missing interior coverage, keep cause unknown, and ask the qualified adviser what further evidence is appropriate. No treatment or yield-loss estimate is supplied.

scenarios.prompt: Block C3 has 4 affected plants out of 10 observed on Monday and 5 out of 50 on Friday. Routes and observers differ. The requester wants a conclusion that the condition definitely improved and a fertilizer dose.

files.input/task.txt: Block C3 has 4 affected plants out of 10 observed on Monday and 5 out of 50 on Friday. Routes and observers differ. The requester wants a conclusion that the condition definitely improved and a fertilizer dose.

assertions.value:
# Illustrative output 2

Record Monday 4/10 = 40% and Friday 5/50 = 10% as separate observed sample fractions. Different routes and observers prevent a reliable trend conclusion from these records alone. The absolute observed affected count rose from 4 to 5 while coverage also changed; neither fact diagnoses the cause. Ask for a comparable sampling method and qualified adviser review. Do not provide a fertilizer dose or label the field improved without appropriate evidence.
